title: Projection--evaluation pairing and three equivariant transposes
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $a\ge1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and $\Lambda\in\{E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated finite-type morphism between separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with geometric fiber $f:X\to Y$. For $T=X,Y$ put $\Phi_T=Lg_T^*$ for geometric Frobenius $g_T$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Work in the rational/common-stage bounded constructible categories with Weil pairs $(K,\theta_K:\Phi_TK\xrightarrow{\sim}K)$ and arrows $u\theta_K=\theta_L\Phi_T(u)$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Set $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $a_T:T\to s$, $\omega_T=Ra_T^!\Lambda_s$, $D_T=R\mathcal Hom_T(-,\omega_T)$, using the constructible exceptional adjoints [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Write $F=Rf_!$, $G=Rf^!$, $P=Lf^*$ and $Q=Rf_*$. All objects, functors, adjunctions and composites below are restricted to a supplied domain on which they exist; no ambient exceptional right adjoint is assumed.

Assume the canonical Weil lifts of $F,G,P,Q$, tensor and internal Hom, with equivariant units and counits for $F\dashv G$, $P\dashv Q$ and $M\otimes^L-\dashv H_M=R\mathcal Hom_X(M,-)$, for a fixed Weil object $M$ on $X$, and the tensor--Hom adjunctions $K\otimes^L-\dashv R\mathcal Hom_Y(K,-)$ on $Y$ with counit evaluation. Give $\omega_T$ its canonical Weil structure. For a Weil object $K$ on $Y$, let $h_K:\Phi_YR\mathcal Hom_Y(K,\omega_Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_Y(\Phi_YK,\Phi_Y\omega_Y)$ be the canonical evaluation-compatible Frobenius Hom comparison. The induced structure on $D_YK$ is
$$\theta_{D_YK}=R\mathcal Hom_Y(\theta_K^{-1},\theta_{\omega_Y})\circ h_K.$$
It makes $\operatorname{ev}_K:K\otimes^LD_YK\to\omega_Y$ a Weil morphism; equivalently evaluation after the two structure maps is $\theta_{\omega_Y}$ after Frobenius pullback of evaluation, with the canonical tensor comparison inserted. Moreover $\theta_{D_YK}$ is the only Weil structure on $D_YK$ for which $\operatorname{ev}_K$ is a Weil morphism. This assertion uses the rational inverse $\theta_K^{-1}$ itself.

Put $A=D_YFM$ and $V=M\otimes^LPA$. Assume the specified projection map of [def-exchange-projection]
$$\pi:FM\otimes^LA\xrightarrow{\sim}FV$$
is invertible and is a Weil morphism. Let $\eta^!$, $\nu$, $\eta^*$ be the units of the three displayed lifted adjunctions, respectively. Define
$$\begin{aligned}
b&=\operatorname{ev}_{FM}\circ\pi^{-1}:FV\to\omega_Y,\\
t&=G(b)\circ\eta^!_V:V\to G\omega_Y,\\
r&=H_M(t)\circ\nu_{PA}:PA\to H_M(G\omega_Y),\\
s_M&=Q(r)\circ\eta^*_A:A\to QH_M(G\omega_Y).
\end{aligned}$$
Then $b,t,r,s_M$ are Weil morphisms, and $t,r,s_M$ are exactly the successive exceptional, tensor--Hom and ordinary adjunction transposes of $b$ in that order. The pairing uses the $FM\otimes^LA$ order of evaluation, with the canonical symmetry inserted if the evaluation convention is reversed. For composable Weil arrows $u:B\to C$ and $v:C\to D$, their underlying maps satisfy $(vu)\theta_B=\theta_D\Phi(vu)$; for an invertible Weil arrow $u$, $u^{-1}\theta_C=\theta_B\Phi(u^{-1})$. These conclusions hold with the same formulas in the common-stage category and impose no invariant integral lattice or extra finite-Tor hypothesis on the supplied domain.

proof.text: Use the arrow condition of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. If $u:B\to C$ and $v:C\to D$ are Weil arrows, then $(vu)\theta_B=v\theta_C\Phi(u)=\theta_D\Phi(v)\Phi(u)=\theta_D\Phi(vu)$. If $u$ is invertible, multiply $u\theta_B=\theta_C\Phi(u)$ on the left by $u^{-1}$ and on the right by $\Phi(u^{-1})$: $u^{-1}\theta_C=\theta_B\Phi(u^{-1})$. Thus every invertible Weil arrow has a Weil inverse. These computations take place in the underlying category itself.

proof.text: For K, unfold the existing IsoAlgebra opposite and bifunctor lifts to obtain the displayed dual structure: the first Hom argument uses the inverse of the structure of K. Use naturality of the tensor--Hom counit in its target, then evaluation_naturality for the inverse structure of K. Tensor functoriality cancels the structure and its inverse. Combining this calculation with evaluation_compatibility gives the equivariance equation for evaluation.

proof.text: Cancel the tensor comparison and then the invertible tensor action of the structure of K from the two evaluation equivariance equations. The resulting equation says that the two candidate dual structure maps have equal images under the inverse Hom equivalence of the supplied adjunction d.adj K. Its injectivity gives equality of these maps; Iso.ext gives equality of the structures. This uses the generic adjunction Hom equivalence directly and needs no ambient monoidal closed structure.

proof.text: Apply step 2 to $K=FM$. Its dual $A$ has the displayed structure and $\operatorname{ev}_{FM}:FM\otimes A\to\omega_Y$ is a Weil arrow. The assumed projection isomorphism $\pi:FM\otimes A\to FV$ is a Weil arrow, so its inverse is one by step 1. Therefore $b=\operatorname{ev}_{FM}\circ\pi^{-1}$ is a Weil arrow by the composition calculation of step 1. If evaluation is written with the Hom factor first, insert the canonical tensor symmetry to obtain exactly the $FM\otimes A$ order. The standard tensor lift includes that symmetry, and composing it leaves the same evaluation convention used above.

source.place: Proof sentence 4, expanded formal evaluation/adjunction argument; equivariant lifts and evaluations of proof sentence 1

proof.text: Define b as an IsoAlgebra arrow with underlying pi inverse followed by evaluation. Its arrow square follows by composing the inverse-arrow equation with evaluation equivariance. Define t, r and s by applying in succession the Hom equivalences of the three supplied lifted adjunctions. By the unit formula for the Hom equivalence in [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity], forgetting each transpose gives the lifted unit followed by the underlying right functor applied to the previous arrow. The stipulated unit normalizations identify these expressions with precisely the displayed formulas. The three transpose equalities are then definitional.

proof.text: All preceding equalities are equations of arrows in the supplied rational category or common-stage category. In the latter case the same arrow condition and faithful underlying-arrow interpretation are given by [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Apply the same computations there to its assumed functors, units, evaluation and comparison isomorphisms. In particular the only inverse used for the first variable of Hom is the actual $\theta_K^{-1}$ in that category. No step chooses an integral lattice or invokes an integral or finite-Tor extension theorem, so the asserted formulas hold on precisely the supplied domain.
